items.text: Verified network profiles. Both sides agree before any document travels.
Both directions, buying and selling, on one connection.
Company customers and suppliers on one shared party record, with sites, buyers and limits.
Shared links for every kind of document, with no password. Acting on one needs a one-time code.
A partner can join from a link, and the documents you shared are offered into their new books.
Your purchase order arrives as their incoming order, with confirmations and change requests back.
Their delivery note becomes your expected receipt.
Their invoice becomes your draft bill, matched to the order and the receipt.
Credit notes, returns, remittance advice and statements both sides can agree.
Catalogues, requests for quotation and shared quality documents.
Every arrival is a draft. Auto-accept is off by default.
Item maps by barcode, then supplier code, then by hand, remembered for next time.
A thread on every document, and disputes with an owner and an outcome.
Netting what you and a partner owe each other, and network reports.
Companies in one group trade over the network into intercompany accounts.
Peppol and EDI, carried as translations of the same documents.
Exchange documents over AS2, SFTP and value-added networks.

faq.q: Does my partner need to use Clafina?
faq.a: Not to start. You can share any document as a link they open without a password. If they join from the link, the documents you shared are offered into their new books.

faq.q: Can a partner's document change my books without me seeing it?
faq.a: No. Every document that arrives is a draft until you accept it. Auto-accept is off unless you turn it on.

faq.q: Does money move over the network?
faq.a: No. Remittance advice tells your partner what you paid, and netting agrees what you owe each other. The payment itself is made the way you pay today.
